# How to Choose the Right CRM for Your Startup in 2025

 November 9, 2025 7 min read CRM, SaaS

## Introduction

Startups depend on the right CRM to organize contacts, automate follow-ups, and scale revenue without burning runway, yet choosing among HubSpot, Zoho, Salesforce, Pipedrive, and emerging players requires matching features, pricing, and complexity to your stage [web:41][web:48]. The market spans free tiers for pre-seed founders to enterprise suites with AI-powered forecasting, so understanding your current team size, sales process, and integration needs prevents costly migrations later [web:41][web:45]. Peer reviews on platforms like PCMag and G2 highlight usability, customization depth, and support quality as decision factors beyond headline pricing [web:42].

## Why startups need a CRM

A CRM shifts your customer data from scattered spreadsheets and email threads into a centralized system that tracks every interaction, automates repetitive tasks, and surfaces insights for closing deals faster [web:41][web:48]. Early-stage founders use CRMs as personal productivity tools to stay organized, while seed-stage teams leverage automation, pipeline visibility, and marketing integrations to align sales and operations without enterprise overhead [web:48]. The right CRM scales with you—simple enough for managing your first hundred contacts yet powerful for complex pipelines as you grow revenue and headcount [web:45].

## Top CRM options for startups

### HubSpot CRM

HubSpot offers a robust free tier and discounts up to 90% for qualifying startups in their first year, making it a popular choice for pre-seed and seed-stage companies [web:41][web:54]. The free plan includes contact management, deal tracking, email integration, and basic reporting for unlimited users, while paid Starter tiers begin at $20/user/month and unlock marketing automation, landing pages, and custom workflows [web:51][web:58]. HubSpot’s 2025 pricing introduces standalone CRM Professional at $50/user/month and Enterprise at $75/user/month, though existing customers retain access to Smart CRM at no extra charge with any Hub purchase [web:55]. This pricing flexibility and end-to-end tooling—from sales to marketing to customer service—positions HubSpot as an all-in-one platform for startups aiming to unify their go-to-market stack [web:41][web:55].

### Zoho CRM

Zoho CRM delivers automation, AI assistant Zia, and deep integrations at a fraction of enterprise CRM costs, ideal for seed-stage teams that need scalable systems without exhausting runway [web:48][web:56]. The forever-free plan supports up to three users with lead, contact, and deal management plus mobile apps, while the Standard plan at $20/user/month (annual billing) adds sales forecasting and workflows [web:56][web:59]. Professional at $35/user/month includes inventory management and advanced customization, Enterprise at $50/user/month provides sandboxing and unlimited reports, and Ultimate at $65/user/month offers unlimited dashboards and premium support [web:56][web:59]. Zoho’s affordability and feature depth help small teams operate like larger organizations, bridging the gap from personal productivity to cross-functional alignment as you scale [web:48][web:56].

### Salesforce

Salesforce remains the enterprise standard with extensive customization, a massive AppExchange marketplace, and robust reporting, though its complexity and cost often exceed early-stage startup needs [web:45][web:60]. Effective August 1, 2025, Salesforce raised Enterprise Edition to $165/user/month (up 6% on average) and Unlimited Edition to $330/user/month, while Starter/Essentials holds at $25/user/month and Professional at $80/user/month [web:57][web:60]. New Agentforce 1 Editions start at $550/user/month for comprehensive AI and analytics, targeting mid-market and enterprise buyers with advanced agentic capabilities [web:57]. Startups on tight budgets may find Salesforce overkill initially but should consider it as they approach Series A and require deep integrations, complex territory management, or industry-specific clouds [web:60].

### Pipedrive

Pipedrive focuses on visual pipeline management with an intuitive interface that sales teams adopt quickly, offering accurate forecasting, AI-powered automation, and 250+ integrations [web:41]. Its strength lies in team collaboration tools, lead segmentation for targeted outreach, and activity reminders that keep reps on track without manual overhead [web:41]. Pipedrive’s pricing and feature tiers suit small to mid-sized sales teams that prioritize ease of use and rapid onboarding over extensive customization [web:41].

### Bitrix24

Bitrix24 provides a free CRM with social media and email integrations, analytics, staff management dashboards, and collaboration tools, available as SaaS, on-premise, or open source [web:41]. The basic package includes custom fields, a free call center, and 5GB online storage, plus an HR management tool that helps young companies streamline hiring [web:41]. This makes Bitrix24 a versatile, low-cost option for bootstrapped startups needing CRM, collaboration, and HR in one platform [web:41].

## Choosing by stage

### Pre-seed: Free tiers and simplicity

At pre-seed, prioritize free CRMs like HubSpot or Zoho that offer contact management, deal tracking, and mobile access without upfront costs, letting you validate product-market fit before investing in paid tiers [web:48][web:54]. Look for intuitive interfaces that require minimal setup so you spend time selling, not configuring fields and workflows [web:48]. HubSpot’s unlimited-user free plan and Zoho’s three-user free tier both provide essential building blocks to stay organized as you land your first customers [web:54][web:56].

### Seed: Automation and integrations

By seed stage, your CRM must automate follow-ups, score leads, and integrate with marketing tools to align sales and operations as you scale headcount [web:48]. Zoho CRM’s Standard or Professional plans deliver workflow automation and Zia AI insights at $20–$35/user/month, while HubSpot Starter at $20/user/month adds email sequences and landing pages for inbound lead capture [web:51][web:56]. Evaluate which integrations—Slack, Google Workspace, Zapier, or accounting software—your team depends on, and confirm native connectors or robust API support before committing [web:41][web:45].

### Series A and beyond: Customization and scale

Post-Series A, consider platforms like Salesforce or higher HubSpot tiers that support complex territory rules, custom objects, advanced reporting, and role-based permissions for larger go-to-market teams [web:45][web:60]. Salesforce’s AppExchange and customization depth suit companies with unique processes or vertical-specific requirements, though implementation and admin costs rise accordingly [web:60]. HubSpot’s Professional and Enterprise Hubs offer marketing attribution, predictive lead scoring, and dedicated support for scaling inbound operations [web:55].

## Key features to evaluate

### Contact and pipeline management

Ensure your CRM provides a clear visual pipeline—Kanban-style boards or customizable stages—so reps understand deal status at a glance and managers forecast revenue accurately [web:41][web:45]. Contact profiles should consolidate email history, call logs, notes, and activity timelines in one view, reducing context switching and manual data entry [web:41].

### Automation and AI

Look for workflow automation that triggers follow-up emails, assigns leads by territory, or updates deal stages based on actions, freeing reps to focus on high-value conversations [web:45][web:56]. AI assistants like Zoho’s Zia or HubSpot’s predictive scoring analyze historical data to suggest optimal contact times, forecast deal outcomes, and surface at-risk opportunities [web:45][web:56].

### Integrations and ecosystem

Validate that your CRM connects to your email provider, calendar, marketing automation, support desk, and accounting systems via native integrations or Zapier [web:41][web:45]. A rich ecosystem—HubSpot’s App Marketplace, Salesforce’s AppExchange, or Zoho’s 50+ app suite—extends functionality without custom development [web:45][web:55].

### Reporting and analytics

Basic dashboards should display pipeline value, win rates, sales cycle length, and rep activity, while advanced plans offer custom reports, cohort analysis, and revenue attribution [web:41][web:56]. Real-time dashboards and drag-and-drop report builders let non-technical users answer business questions without waiting on engineering [web:45].

### Mobile access

Mobile apps for iOS and Android ensure reps log calls, update deals, and access contact details on the go, critical for field sales or remote teams [web:56]. Check that mobile functionality mirrors desktop capabilities rather than offering a stripped-down experience [web:56].

## Pricing comparison table

| CRM | Free Plan | Entry Paid | Mid Tier | Enterprise | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HubSpot | Yes, unlimited users | $20/user/mo (Starter) | $50/user/mo (Pro CRM) | $75/user/mo (Enterprise CRM) | 90% discount for qualifying startups first year [web:51][web:55] |
| Zoho CRM | Yes, 3 users | $20/user/mo (Standard) | $35/user/mo (Professional) | $50/user/mo (Enterprise) | AI Zia included in Professional+ [web:56][web:59] |
| Salesforce | No | $25/user/mo (Essentials) | $80/user/mo (Professional) | $165/user/mo (Enterprise) | 6% increase effective Aug 2025 [web:57][web:60] |
| Pipedrive | 14-day trial | Varies by plan | Varies by plan | Varies by plan | 250+ integrations, visual pipeline focus [web:41] |
| Bitrix24 | Yes | Paid tiers available | Paid tiers available | Paid tiers available | Includes HR tools, call center, 5GB storage [web:41] |

## Common mistakes to avoid

Do not over-customize your CRM upfront—start with standard fields and workflows, then iterate based on actual sales team feedback to prevent configuration bloat that slows adoption [web:45]. Avoid choosing a CRM solely on brand recognition or feature count; instead, run a pilot with your sales team using real data to confirm usability and fit before rolling out company-wide [web:45]. Resist the temptation to migrate CRMs frequently, as each switch incurs data cleanup, retraining, and integration rework that distracts from revenue activities [web:48].

## Final recommendations

For pre-seed founders managing initial customer conversations, start with HubSpot’s free CRM for unlimited users and straightforward setup, or Zoho Free if you have three or fewer users and want AI preview [web:54][web:56]. Seed-stage teams seeking affordable automation should evaluate Zoho CRM Standard or Professional for advanced workflows and integrations at $20–$35/user/month, or HubSpot Starter if inbound marketing and landing pages matter [web:51][web:56]. Post-Series A companies with complex sales processes and budget for implementation should pilot Salesforce Professional or Enterprise, factoring in the August 2025 price increases and AppExchange dependency costs [web:57][web:60]. Ultimately, pick a CRM that your team will actually use daily—intuitive UX, mobile access, and fast support drive adoption far more than feature checklists [web:41][web:45].

## CRM setup & configuration FAQs

### How much does CRM setup cost?

US clients pay $800 to $4,000 and Australian clients pay A$1,200 to A$6,000. A single pipeline on HubSpot Starter with 500 migrated contacts sits at the low end. Salesforce with custom objects, several teams, and complex automation sits at the top.

### How long does setup take?

Two to four weeks for most small and mid-sized teams. Data migration is usually the longest task, especially when the old records are inconsistent or duplicated.

### Who owns the CRM account and the data in it?

You do. The account is in your company name on your billing. We work as a guest admin and are removed once you are comfortable running it.

### What happens after launch?

The first month is when people actually learn the system, so we stay reachable for questions and small fixes. After that, most clients want a quarterly tune-up rather than constant involvement.

### Which CRM should we pick?

HubSpot suits small sales teams that want to start quickly and keep costs low. Zoho is cheaper at scale and covers more back-office functions. Salesforce is worth the cost when your process is genuinely complex or you need deep customisation. Picking before mapping your process is how teams end up with an expensive tool nobody uses.

### Will our old data migrate cleanly?

Rarely without work. Duplicate contacts, missing fields, and inconsistent stage names are normal. We clean and de-duplicate during migration and give you a report of what could not be mapped instead of dropping rows quietly.

### Do you charge per user?

No, our fee is for the setup work. Your CRM vendor charges per user per month, and that cost scales with your team. We give you the vendor pricing before you commit so there are no surprises.

# Pipedrive Pricing and Plans: Which One Is Right for You?

Not sure which Pipedrive plan is right for you? We’ve prepared a clear comparison of all plans so you can easily see which one will best support your business.

## Pipedrive Pricing Plans

Pipedrive’s subscription packages offer different levels of efficiency, automation, and simplification for your work. Thanks to recent positive changes, we can now provide you with even greater value—at the same or even lower prices than before.

Currently, there are 5 plans available: 

*The listed price is per user with annual billing

Image: Pipedrive Plans – Annual Pricing 2025

*The listed price is per user with monthly billing

Image: Pipedrive Plans – Monthly Pricing 2025

Let’s take a look at how these plans differ and how to choose the one that best fits your needs!

## Comparison of Individual Pipedrive Plans

Choose the right plan primarily based on your company’s needs and how you intend to use your CRM. Explore a comparison of all Pipedrive plans – from the basic Lite version to the most advanced option, Dáváme Ultimate.

### Lite Plan

The Lite plan gives you everything you’d expect from a CRM, plus a range of AI-powered features – making AI your new team partner. You’ll also have access to Pulse Feed (a stream of priorities) and receive a free onboarding call with a Dáváme consultant, who will tailor Pipedrive to your specific business needs.

| Key Features | All essential CRM functionalities AI integration Pulse Feed – an organized overview of opportunities, missed deals, and follow-up actions Free onboarding session with a Dáváme consultant | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best For | CRM beginners with minimal needs (e.g., freelancers or small agencies with up to 5 people who want to switch from Excel and start managing sales more effectively). | |
| Pricing | 24 EUR per user/month monthly billing | 14 EUR per user/month annual billing |

### Growth Plan

The Growth plan includes everything from the Lite plan and adds tools that significantly boost team efficiency. It offers full email integration and synchronization with Pipedrive CRM, as well as the ability to create automations and sequences that take over a large portion of daily or repetitive tasks. In addition, it lets you schedule meetings, emails, and video calls directly, and provides ready-made predictive reports so you always have an overview of subscriptions and forecasted revenue.

| Key Features | Full email synchronization with Pipedrive Integration with Google/Microsoft contacts and calendar Customizable email templates and signatures Automations Sequences for lead nurturing Pre-built reports and dashboards | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best For | Small teams looking to save time with automation and handle a larger volume of emails. Ideal for sales teams in startups or real estate agencies where multiple deals need to be managed simultaneously and repetitive tasks automated. | |
| Pricing | 49 EUR per user/month monthly billing | 39 EUR per user/month annual billing |

### Premium Plan

Premium is the most popular plan overall, building on the foundation of the Growth plan and expanding it with advanced sales management tools. It provides comprehensive support for the entire sales process – from the first contact to deal closure and project delivery.

As a full "end-to-end" solution, it includes a complete set of tools for lead generation and scoring, nurturing potential customers, automatic lead assignment, contract management, electronic signatures, and even project management. You’ll also benefit from AI-powered email, advanced team management, and customizable fields.

Thanks to its complexity and flexibility, Premium is a favorite choice for companies of all sizes.

| Key Features | Lead generation and routing Custom scoring setup Company data enrichment Contract management tools and eSignatures Ability to configure custom, mandatory, and advanced fields Advanced options for previously basic features (automations, reporting, email templates, etc.) API access and webhooks Enhanced security Fully customizable visibility groups and permissions | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Best For | Growing companies with multiple salespeople and managers who want to track performance and goal achievement, improve collaboration, or need to manage multiple departments or sales processes. | |
| Pricing | 79 EUR per user/month monthly billing | 1 250 Kč (49 Eur) per user/month annual billing |

### Ultimate Plan

The Ultimate plan unlocks absolutely every feature Pipedrive has to offer – there’s nothing beyond it. It provides the maximum limits across all tools and, compared to the Premium plan, adds enhanced security, data enrichment not only for organizations but also for individual contacts, plus a sandbox account for safe testing without the risk of affecting live data.

| Hlavní funkce | Full access to all Pipedrive CRM features Stronger account security with rules and alerts Data enrichment for individuals (not just organizations) Maximum limits on restricted features Sandbox testing environment | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ideální pro | Larger teams, companies with higher security requirements, or organizations with complex, company-wide needs. | |
| Cena | 99 EUR per user/month monthly billing | 79 EUR per user/month annual billing |

### Dáváme Ultimate Plan

Dáváme Ultimate is an exclusive plan available only to our clients. In addition to the full range of Pipedrive features, it also gives you all the benefits provided by Dáváme – including our 24/7 priority support. This means your questions will always be resolved immediately, without any waiting.

| Hlavní funkce | Full access to all Pipedrive CRM features Stronger account security with rules and alerts Data enrichment for individuals (not just organizations) Maximum limits on restricted features Sandbox testing environment Priority support from Dáváme 24/7 availability | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ideální pro | Larger teams or companies with higher or more complex needs that require immediate answers to their questions, without the usual delays caused by limited business hours or support queues. | |
| Cena | 179 EUR per user/month monthly billing | 159 EUR per user/month annual billing |

## Summary

Among our clients, the Premium plan is clearly the most popular – it offers the best price-to-performance ratio and is a perfect fit for companies where the sales department is the heart of the business. The Growth plan is also a favorite, though companies often combine it with external tools. Ultimate achieves strong results as well, attracting those who want the absolute certainty that nothing more can be unlocked – since it offers the complete maximum.

The least common choices are the two extremes – Lite, typically used by CRM beginners, and Dáváme Ultimate, reserved only for the most demanding companies.

If you’re not sure which plan is right for you, get in touch with us! We’ll be happy to discuss your needs and recommend a tailored solution.
